item.title: Cabinet declares HIV outbreak a national crisis
item.description: Mansi Chand , Pita Toganivalu · 10/09/2026 Cabinet has endorsed the declaration of Fiji’s HIV outbreak as a national health crisis as the government moves to strengthen its response to the issue.
item.content:encoded:
Mansi Chand , Pita Toganivalu · 10/09/2026

Cabinet has endorsed the declaration of Fiji’s HIV outbreak as a national health crisis as the government moves to strengthen its response to the issue.

Minister for Information Lynda Tabuya confirmed this after the Cabinet meeting, saying Cabinet extensively discussed a paper on Fiji’s HIV response and received further information from Dr Jason Mitchell and his team.

T abuya says they are declaring it a national crisis under emergency powers and it is important for Fiji to respond accordingly.

She says the government is taking the issue very seriously , with funding being provided through Fiji’s development partners as well as the national budget.

Tabuya says the Ministry of Health already has a dedicated unit focused on responding to the HIV crisis.

item.title: WATCH: Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist Dr Nanise Sikiti share her story on fijivillage Her-Story
item.description: From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji's first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti's journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination. Dr Sikiti shares her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono.
item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji's first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti's journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti shares her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono.

Dr Sikiti also shares the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She speaks about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.
